input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 grants termination only for material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and security/SLA/law/IP failures (9.3); Sections 6.2, 19.4 and 27.3 are likewise cause-based exits. Neither Party has a convenience right, and Section 2.1 affirmatively strips termination rights across the three-year take-or-pay commitment, so Customer is locked into a multi-year term with no convenience exit - walk-away territory under the rule and a failure of the fallback too. Section 8.2 non-renewal is natural-term expiry and is not flagged here. Vendor holds no convenience right today, but the rule requires that to be stated affirmatively, so new Section 9.4 grants Customer a 30-day convenience exit with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and bars Vendor convenience termination during a committed term; the Section 2.1 edit removes only the termination-rights bar and leaves the volume-reduction restriction intact.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.

proposal.summary: Add Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; bar Vendor convenience termination; conform take-or-pay clause.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a Customer right to terminate for convenience on thirty days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and confirmed Vendor has no convenience exit during a committed term. We also conformed Section 2.1, which otherwise removed all termination rights during the three-year commitment; the volume-reduction restriction is unchanged. If helpful, our fallback is 60-90 days' notice with an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.
